newsitem.title: EGYPT: Cairo Housing goes majority private.
newsitem.headline: Cairo Housing goes majority private.

text.p: The Egyptian state sold the private sector more than two million shares in Cairo Housing and Development, about 33 percent of the company's equity, on Monday in an operation which puts the company outside state control.

Mohamed Hossny of brokers Triple A Securities, which handled the sale for the state's Holding Company for Housing, Cinema and Tourism, told Reuters the state decided to satisfy all the applications it received for the shares and to sell the shares at the minimum price of 24.72 pounds ($7.28) a share.

The holding company had offered 1.272 million shares, 20 percent of the equity, in a privatisation and it received applications for 2,079,853 shares. The transaction went through the stock exchange on Monday.
Hossny described the privatisation as a great success given the recent slump in prices on the Egyptian stock market and a widespread feeling that the offer might be undersubscribed.

The private sector now owns 65 percent of Cairo Housing, including the 10 percent held by the employee shareholders association. The holding company retains 27.4 percent and two insurance companies hold the balance, Hossny said.
The state had sold some shares to the private sector earlier in the privatisation programme, which began in 1993.
Hossny said he thought the price struck was fair to both buyers and the seller. It was significantly higher than the valuation by the government's audit office, he added.

Cairo Housing raised net after-tax profit to 5.355 million pounds in the financial year 1995/96 from 2.947 million pounds in the previous year. It expects the profit to increase to 10.624 million in 1996/97. The financial year ends on June 30.
The firm distributed a dividend of 0.53 pounds in 1995/96.
